correctness.rationale: The domain contains every constant function, so the source's pointwise transfer lemma applies and yields ZFC. For every lambda >= kappa, the function taking lambda at one state and lambda-plus elsewhere lies in the size cut and is strictly between the endpoints. For lambda < kappa, any nonconstant cardinal in the domain has all coordinates at least kappa, while a candidate intermediate must be pointwise at most lambda-plus <= kappa; equality at the boundary forces the function to be constant. GCH identifies the upper endpoint with the power-set cardinal.

value.rationale: The theorem classifies the existence of intermediate cardinal profiles throughout all infinite-cardinal intervals in a motivated size-cut domain. It shows that the boundary changes exactly from lambda > kappa in the rank cut to lambda >= kappa in the size cut, even though both filtered domains satisfy ZFC. The scope is a complete threshold classification for this one filtration, not a classification of all filtrations.
